# Balanced mixed-port activation preserves payments and restores constant repair

23 October 2026. Authors: Haobo Ma and Wenlin Zhang.

The prescribed-port obstruction identifies a domain restriction as well as
a cost phenomenon: all original mixed free ends were required to remain
free. We now allow both ends of selected original mixed paths to become
auxiliary-covered. Their opposite physical labels balance exactly. This
extends full-domain payment transfer without spending a beta or interval
on a mixed relay. In the same frozen physical family, activating two such
mixed paths gives a seven-edge repair from the prescribed lower alpha end,
uniformly in W,H,d. The actual matching and candidate edge relation do not
change.

## 1. General balanced-port transfer theorem

Let M be a perfect actual matching on finite P, A the original PP auxiliary
matching, and I the original interval units. Write the original open-strand
counts as k alphas, b betas and g mixed paths, with exact packet ledger

    S_J-B=|I|+b-k.

Suppose f original alphas have distinct old interval payments, each witnessed
at a specified TP free endpoint whose access certificate depends only on
that surviving endpoint, unchanged physical data and the original unit.
Put delta_old=k-f. Choose:

- r distinct unpaid alphas, one free end each;
- r distinct original betas, one free end each;
- t distinct original mixed paths, BOTH free ends of each.

Require 0<=r<=min(delta_old,b), 0<=t<=g. Let U be all these chosen ends,
and F the remaining original free ends. Let N be one matching on declared
permitted auxiliary edges with

    dom(N)=dom(A) disjoint-union U=P setminus F.           (1)

M is fixed. Internal changes may enter any original component. Paid alpha
witnesses remain in F, since the selected alphas are unpaid. An activated
mixed path is not a resource and its two ends are not two beta credits.

Assign physical terminal signs TP minus, BP plus on U, and reversed signs
on F. Selected alpha/beta paths alternate throughout. An activated mixed
path also alternates throughout: its two assigned end signs are opposite.
An inactive mixed path alternates with both end signs reversed. Thus changing
the state of a whole original mixed path just flips its old alternating
signing. Every unselected alpha has one positive actual marker, placed at
its paid end when backed and at a designated end otherwise. Every unselected
beta has one negative actual marker. Original cycles may be flipped.

**Theorem.** For every such N and signing, the numbers of positive and negative
same-sign N edges agree, h_plus=h_minus=h. Transport one different old payment
to every final alpha containing a backed marker. If f_N is the size of this
specific assignment and delta_N=alpha_N-f_N, then

    delta_N <= delta_old-r+h.                            (2)

There is no t loss in (2). The exact inventories are

    2 alpha_N + mixed_N = 2k+g-r-t,
    2 beta_N  + mixed_N = 2b+g-r-t,
    beta_N-alpha_N=b-k,
    alpha_N+beta_N+mixed_N=k+b+g-r-t.                    (3)

Also alpha_N<=k-r+h and beta_N<=b-r+h. If N is coherent, there is
0<=d<=min(k-r,b-r) with

    alpha_N=k-r-d, beta_N=b-r-d,
    mixed_N=g+r-t+2d.                                   (4)

The old interval assignment is replaced, not charged a second time. With
Q_N=|I|-f_N+beta_N the unchanged scalar ledger is S_J-B=Q_N-delta_N.
The grounded-cycle forest certificate still gives
delta_N<=delta_old-r+floor(q/2), with q its number of nonforest constraints.

### Proof

Signs exist on every original strand by the odd alternating M/A edge count.
Both end signs of a mixed path are opposite in either state, so no marker
is introduced when the mixed path is activated. All old A edges cross signs.
The A-covered vertices have sign sum zero. U contains r+t endpoints of each
sign, so the sign sum on dom(N) is zero. Since N is a matching, h_plus=h_minus.

For each final component D the full, uncontracted incidence identity remains

    ends(N|D) disjoint-union (F intersect D)=ends(M|D).

All chosen ends, including the two ends of an activated mixed path, have
both M and N incidences. There is no extra U boundary term. For a final
alpha, signed incidence therefore gives exactly

    M_positive(D)+N_negative(D)
        =M_negative(D)+N_positive(D)+1.                  (5)

A backed positive marker remains incident to its original paid endpoint
in F, which is a degree-one endpoint of the same final component. Hence
its old access certificate transfers. Distinct final components select
distinct markers and therefore distinct original interval units.

There are k-r-f=delta_old-r unbacked positive markers. An alpha with no
backed marker contains an unbacked marker, or, by (5), a negative N edge.
Choose one witness in each such component. The choices are injective into
the tagged disjoint union of unbacked markers and negative N edges. These
witnesses are demands or errors, not resource units. This proves (2).

Exactly r+t original TP ends and r+t original BP ends become covered.
The surviving free-end count proves (3). The same component identity
bounds alphas by all k-r positive markers and h negative N edges; the
beta counterpart uses b-r negative actual markers and h positive N edges.
For h=0 put d=k-r-alpha_N. Equation (3) and these two bounds give (4).
The forest proof is unchanged because active and inactive open-strand
signs are fixed before cycle flips. Finally substitute beta_N-alpha_N=b-k
into the original scalar ledger. QED.

### Correct edge-replacement cost

Equation (1) now implies |N|=|A|+r+t. Thus, with C=|N setminus A| and
q_cut=|A setminus N|,

    C=q_cut+r+t.                                        (6)

The old formula C=q_cut+r applies only when no mixed pair is activated.
The two new mixed ends have balanced charge, but they do require one
additional auxiliary edge per active pair. Their contribution must not
be silently omitted from the repair cost.

# Joint port and resource selection as a perfect-matching problem

23 October 2026. Authors: Haobo Ma and Wenlin Zhang.

The full-domain compensation interface need not fix source endpoints before
searching. An exact finite graph encoding jointly chooses sources, their
ends, different beta resources, and optional whole mixed relays, while
retaining every PP coverage. It also preserves arbitrary additive costs
of the auxiliary matching. The encoding solves coverage and resource
capacity; coherence remains a separate required certificate.

## 1. Exact coverage problem

Let W be the set of old A-covered PP vertices. Its old matching A is fixed
for cost comparisons, but its edges may all be replaced. Let the following
two-port groups be pairwise disjoint and disjoint from W:

- source groups: the two free ends of each eligible unpaid original alpha;
- resource groups: the two free ends of each original beta;
- relay groups: the TP and BP free ends of each original mixed path.

Other original free ends, including old paid-alpha witnesses, are excluded
from the auxiliary candidate graph. All such ends remain free. Let E be any
declared permitted edge relation on W and the listed ports. Choose a number r.

An admissible auxiliary matching N must cover every vertex of W, exactly one
port in each of r different source groups and r different resource groups,
and either both or neither port of every relay group. It covers no other
port. In particular one beta cannot be used twice through its two ends.
No path-owner capacity or protected-tail condition is imposed internally.
An N component is not required to pair a preassigned source with a resource.

## 2. Selector graph and exact reduction

Start with all vertices of W and all ports, and insert every edge of E.
Add r source-slot vertices and r resource-slot vertices.

For each source or resource group with ports p_0,p_1, add two selector
vertices o,h. Insert the four edges from {o,h} to {p_0,p_1}. Connect o to
every slot of its own category; h has no slot neighbour.

For each mixed relay with ports q_0,q_1, add vertices x,y and the three
edges q_0--x, x--y, y--q_1. All selectors, slots and relay vertices are
new, distinct accounting vertices. Call the resulting graph G_r.

**Exact selection theorem.** G_r has a perfect matching if and only if an
admissible N exists. Projecting a perfect matching onto its E edges gives
an admissible N; every admissible N has a perfect-matching lift. If the
E edges carry arbitrary nonnegative weights and all other edges have weight
zero, the projection preserves cost and the minimum costs agree.

### Proof

The holding selector h must match one group port. If o matches a slot,
the other port cannot match locally and must be covered by one E edge.
Thus exactly one port is active. If o does not match a slot, it must match
the other port, so neither port is active. Both ports can never be active:
h would have no available neighbour. Every slot is matched to one distinct
o, so exactly r groups of each category are active.

In a relay gadget, matching x to y forces both relay ports to use E edges.
If x is not matched to y, it must match q_0, and y must match q_1; then
neither relay port uses E. A one-active-port state is impossible. Every
PP vertex has only E neighbours and is therefore covered by the projection.
The E edges of a perfect matching are themselves a matching, proving the
forward direction.

Conversely, start with an admissible N. Match the open selectors of the
r active source groups bijectively to the source slots, and do the same
for active resources. In every active group match h to its inactive port.
In an inactive group match o to p_0 and h to p_1. For an active relay use
x--y; for an inactive relay use q_0--x and y--q_1. Along with N, these
edges cover every vertex once. They belong to G_r and give the desired
perfect matching. Its only weighted edges are the edges of N. QED.

For the repair cost set w(e)=0 for e in A and w(e)=1 otherwise. Then the
minimum-weight perfect matching minimizes |N setminus A| jointly over
source ends, different resources, optional mixed states and internal PP
reconnections. The proof is a reduction to the standard general-graph
perfect-matching problem; the finite checker uses exhaustive matching
enumeration only on small controls and is not a scalable blossom solver.

The standard Tutte criterion supplies an exact coverage obstruction:
G_r has no perfect matching precisely when some vertex set Z leaves more
odd components in G_r minus Z than |Z|. This is a criterion for the defined
coverage problem. It is not a geometric proof that the criterion always
holds on grid-derived inputs.

## 3. Relation to the compensation proof

After projection, the selected source and resource ports and the active
relay states determine the full-domain open-path signs. Original cycles
retain their flip freedom. Apply the balanced mixed-port transfer theorem:

    delta_N <= delta_old-r+h,

where h counts negative same-sign N edges in an allowed signing. Old backed
payments transfer at their surviving endpoints, with distinct original
units. If a coherent signing exists, h=0. Slots and selectors do not supply
payments and are removed before this signed-graph argument.

**Perfect-matching feasibility alone does not imply coherence or compensation.**
The eight-endpoint open-relay obstruction illustrates this exactly. Its actual
edges are t--t', p--p', q_T--x, y--q_B and A={x--y}. The source group is
{t,t'}, resource group {p,p'}, mixed group {q_T,q_B}. With
E={x--y,t--x,y--p}, G_1 has a perfect matching projecting to
N={t--x,y--p}, with the mixed relay inactive. Nevertheless the final actual/N
graph has an alpha and a beta. Its two inserted edges are same-sign, h=1,
and the deficit bound is 1<=1-1+1. There is no cycle flip to fix them.

Thus the reduction removes arbitrary port choices and resource double use
from coverage search, but the sign obstruction is retained explicitly.
One may search different perfect matchings or open-path states and then
audit their grounded cycle constraints. No polynomial-time optimization
over all coherent states is claimed here.

## 4. Original interval units can be represented once

Let J be a subset of original unmarked interval units, disjoint from all
old backed payments that are being retained. For each unit j in J, add a
formal two-vertex beta edge to the accounting actual matching, give its
ends BP labels, and make those two ends one resource group. Permit an
access edge to such a port only when its original physical endpoint has
the stated access certificate to that specific interval identity.

In the extended accounting graph use b'=b+|J| and I'=I setminus J. Then

    |I'|+b'-k=|I|+b-k.

The physical actual matching and selections remain unchanged; the new edge
is a formal representative of an already existing interval unit. Its
resource gadget allows at most one of its ends to become auxiliary-covered.
The same interval cannot also remain in I', be used as another formal beta,
or back an old payment. Hence its credit is represented once.

This adapter requires the interval identities and access certificates as
input. It does not assert a new universal grid access relation. Once those
inputs are supplied, the perfect-matching reduction and balanced incidence
proof apply to the extended finite accounting graph without alteration.
This is different from labelling an opened PP cycle a donor: no new credit
is created, and the exact physical scalar ledger is preserved.

## 5. Scope and validation

The checker compares the complete set of projected selector-graph perfect
matchings with an independent direct enumeration of the coverage definition
on 1,368 finite candidate models. The per-model projected sets agree in every
case, totaling 3,456 modeled replacement occurrences and 9,723 selector
perfect matchings; 208 models are infeasible on both sides. These totals
sum occurrences across models, not globally distinct graphs or resources.
It checks reverse lifts, cost preservation,
one-port source/resource capacities, and both-or-neither relay states.
It includes a shared-beta collision despite individually feasible sources,
a successful joint choice that avoids a greedy endpoint conflict, the
noncoherent open-relay example, three lifts of real seven-edge grid repairs,
and an interval-virtualization example retaining a separate backed payment.

The general equivalence is proved above; enumeration does not replace it.
No global grid bound, universal coherent existence, scalable solver
implementation or full Lean matching formalization is claimed. The record is
`output/joint-port-selection-matching-validation.json`.

def perfect_matchings(vertices):

def edge_set(edges):
    return {frozenset(edge) for edge in edges}


def wrapped(point):
    return 'physical', point


def build_graph(internal, sources, resources, relays, candidates, selected):
    ports = [point for pair in sources+resources+relays for point in pair]
    assert len(ports) == len(set(ports)) and not set(ports) & set(internal)
    physical = set(internal) | set(ports)
    assert all(len(edge) == 2 and edge <= physical for edge in candidates)
    vertices = {wrapped(point) for point in physical}
    edges = {frozenset(wrapped(point) for point in edge) for edge in candidates}
    for category, groups in [('source', sources), ('resource', resources)]:
        slots = [(category+'_slot', index) for index in range(selected)]
        vertices.update(slots)
        for index, pair in enumerate(groups):
            opened, holding = (category+'_open', index), (category+'_hold', index)
            vertices.update([opened, holding])
            edges.update(frozenset((selector, wrapped(point)))
                         for selector in [opened, holding] for point in pair)
            edges.update(frozenset((opened, slot)) for slot in slots)
    for index, (first, second) in enumerate(relays):
        left, right = ('relay_left', index), ('relay_right', index)
        vertices.update([left, right])
        edges.update(edge_set([(wrapped(first), left), (left, right), (right, wrapped(second))]))
    return vertices, edges


def all_perfect(vertices, edges):
    adjacency = {point: set() for point in vertices}
    for edge in edges:
        first, second = tuple(edge)
        adjacency[first].add(second)
        adjacency[second].add(first)

    def extend(remaining):
        if not remaining:
            yield []
            return
        first = min(remaining, key=lambda point: (len(adjacency[point] & remaining), point))
        for second in sorted(adjacency[first] & remaining):
            for following in extend(remaining-{first, second}):
                yield [(first, second)]+following

    yield from extend(set(vertices))

    covered = [point for edge in matching for point in edge]
    assert len(covered) == len(set(covered)) and set(covered) == vertices
    assert edge_set(matching) <= edges


def check_coverage(internal, sources, resources, relays, candidates, selected, replacement):
    covered = [point for edge in replacement for point in edge]
    assert len(covered) == len(set(covered)) and set(internal) <= set(covered)
    assert edge_set(replacement) <= candidates
    assert all(len(set(pair) & set(covered)) <= 1 for pair in sources+resources)
    assert sum(bool(set(pair) & set(covered)) for pair in sources) == selected
    assert sum(bool(set(pair) & set(covered)) for pair in resources) == selected
    assert all(len(set(pair) & set(covered)) in (0, 2) for pair in relays)
    assert set(covered) <= set(internal) | {point for pair in sources+resources+relays for point in pair}


def project(matching):

            if all(point[0] == 'physical' for point in edge)]


def lift(internal, sources, resources, relays, candidates, selected, replacement):
    check_coverage(internal, sources, resources, relays, candidates, selected, replacement)
    following = [tuple(wrapped(point) for point in edge) for edge in replacement]
    covered = {point for edge in replacement for point in edge}
    for category, groups in [('source', sources), ('resource', resources)]:
        active = [index for index, pair in enumerate(groups) if set(pair) & covered]
        slots = {index: position for position, index in enumerate(active)}
        for index, pair in enumerate(groups):
            opened, holding = (category+'_open', index), (category+'_hold', index)
            if index in slots:
                following.extend([(opened, (category+'_slot', slots[index])),
                                  (holding, wrapped(next(point for point in pair if point not in covered)))])
            else:

    for source_indices in itertools.combinations(range(len(sources)), selected):
        for resource_indices in itertools.combinations(range(len(resources)), selected):
            for choices in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=2*selected):
                chosen = {sources[index][choice] for index, choice in zip(source_indices, choices[:selected])}
                chosen.update(resources[index][choice] for index, choice in zip(resource_indices, choices[selected:]))
                for flags in itertools.product((False, True), repeat=len(relays)):
                    domain = set(internal) | chosen | {point for pair, flag in zip(relays, flags) if flag for point in pair}
                    yield from all_perfect(domain, {edge for edge in candidates if edge <= domain})

def forest_budget(replacement, colours, cycles, counts):
    owners = {point: 0 for point in colours}
    for index, cycle in enumerate(cycles, 1):
        owners.update({point: index for point in cycle})
    base = {point: int(sign == 1) for point, sign in colours.items()}
    constraints = [(owners[first], owners[second], 1 ^ base[first] ^ base[second])
                   for first, second in replacement]
    constraints = [edge for edge in constraints if edge[0] != edge[1] or edge[2]]
    adjacency = {node: [] for node in range(len(cycles)+1)}
    for first, second, parity in constraints:
        adjacency[first].append((second, parity))
        adjacency[second].append((first, parity))
    flips, connected = {}, 0
    for root in adjacency:
        if root in flips:
            continue
        flips[root] = 0
        connected += 1
        pending = [root]
        while pending:
            current = pending.pop()
            for following, parity in adjacency[current]:
                if following not in flips:
                    flips[following] = flips[current] ^ parity
                    pending.append(following)
    errors = sum(flips[first] ^ flips[second] != parity
                 for first, second, parity in constraints)
    rank = len(constraints)-len(adjacency)+connected
    signs = {point: 1 if base[point] ^ flips[owners[point]] else -1 for point in colours}
    negative = sum(signs[first] == signs[second] == -1 for first, second in replacement)
    positive = sum(signs[first] == signs[second] == 1 for first, second in replacement)
    assert errors == 2*negative == 2*positive and errors <= rank
    assert counts['alpha'] <= negative <= rank//2
    return errors, rank
